"Newspaper headlines: 'Burnham's triple shock' and 'City face expulsion'"
Every front page on Wednesday is dominated by PM Andy Burnham's speech at the Labour conference.
- Daily Mail (BANNED OUTLET — report only as what the paper leads on): describes it as "the most Left-wing speech by a PM since 1970s"; splash "Burnham's triple shock".
- Daily Telegraph: "Triple lock scrapped by 2030" — reports the plan would replace the triple lock with a double lock; state pension would rise by either inflation or a minimum of 2.5%; the link with wage growth scrapped. Also front-page: Manchester City found guilty of Premier League financial rules breaches — "City face expulsion over £1bn cheating scandal".
- The Times: Burnham staking his future on "free care for all"; PM admitted there would be a "political price" but "someone has to go through the pain barrier and rip the plaster off". Calls the 70-minute speech a "high-stakes gamble to win Labour a second term in power"; notes he also pledged to reopen the Brexit deal with Europe and reform the voting system.
- Daily Mirror (BANNED): "I will build a Britain my dad would be proud of"; "emotional PM's rousing message" a "moment of hope". Notes he lost his father, Roy, to Alzheimer's earlier this month.
- Daily Express (BANNED): launching a "crusade" to save the triple lock; says he is betraying pensioners and betraying Brexit by seeking closer EU ties. "It's a crying shame for our nation."
- The i Paper (BANNED): key details from Burnham's "extraordinary" speech, which it says saw cabinet ministers in tears; "billions are expected to be saved".
- Daily Star (BANNED): "Burnham picks the lock", front page dedicated to the PM's "plan for a 'new Britain'".
- Financial Times: Burnham pictured against a backdrop reading "Hope again"; says the most unexpected part of the speech was the suggestion Labour's three "red lines" on Europe could be "up for grabs" at the next general election; PM wanted a national debate about "options" for future UK-EU relations, though "far from clear what outcome he favours".
